Subject: SIG follow-up — audit logs, retention, and customer access

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the quick SIG intake call yesterday. A couple of items came up from our compliance team related to the audit/logging section of the SIG that we need clarified for our vendor review:

- Can Redwood provide a short statement about what events are logged by default for hosted deployments (auth events, API calls, admin actions, model inference events, system events)?
- What is your default retention period for structured audit logs, and can customers request a longer retention or export?
- For customers with PHI workloads (we are in healthcare), can we get access to our logs (raw JSON) for forensic analysis? If so, are there controls around PII redaction and delivery mechanism (SFTP, secure API, SIEM connectors)?
- Any evidence we can attach to the SIG: sample log extract (redacted), retention policy, or an internal process doc referencing export workflow.

We have a 5/11 submission deadline for the vendor pack. If you can confirm what you can provide and how long it will take to produce the artifacts, that would be great.

Best,
Alyssa

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear list. Quick reply to set expectations: we can provide a redacted sample log extract, our official log retention policy, and guidance on how customers can obtain exports. Monica (security) and Rishi (platform) are looped in and will follow up with the technical details and evidence.

High-level answers:
- Events logged: auth (token grant/refresh/failures), admin console actions, API request/response metadata (headers, timestamps, model id, token usage), onboarding/tenant lifecycle events, and runtime errors. We do not log full prompt text by default into customer-accessible audit logs unless the customer enables request recording for debugging.
- Retention: default hosted retention is 90 days for structured audit logs; we support 1-yr and custom retention for Dedicated/Private deployments via a contract addendum.
- Customer access: we can provide exports via a secure S3 presigned URL or a one-time SFTP drop. For SIEM integrations we support push-to-Splunk/Datadog via HTTPS and can provide a connector config.

Monica/rishi — can you put together: (1) a redacted sample log extract, (2) the retention policy PDF, and (3) a short statement we can paste into the SIG as evidence? Alyssa — if you prefer a short signed statement instead of the raw extract, tell us and we can prioritize that.

I'll follow up after your delivery ETA.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Hi Alyssa — forwarding the internal notes and attached artifacts. See below for the short evidence items and procedures.

Attached: redwood_log_retention_policy_v1.2.pdf, redwood_audit_log_extract_202604.zip (redacted), sig-evidence-mapping.xlsx

Short evidence statement for SIG: "Redwood Inference logs authentication events, API request/response metadata (excluding prompt content by default), administrative console changes, and system-level events. Default retention for structured audit logs in the hosted service is 90 days. Customers may request exports of their audit logs via secure delivery (S3 presigned URLs, one-time SFTP transfer) or configure push-based delivery to supported SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, Sumo Logic). For Dedicated and Private deployments, custom retention terms and dedicated log sinks can be negotiated as part of the contract."

Operational notes / technical details:
- Log format: newline-delimited JSON with common fields: timestamp (ISO8601), tenant_id, event_type, actor_id, resource, request_id, status, metadata (opaque map).
- PII handling: We mask user-identifying fields by default in customer-accessible extracts. Full unmasked logs are retained in internal telemetry for debugging for up to 14 days and are only accessed by SREs under documented escalation procedures.
- Export workflow: customer requests a log export via the Console or by contacting support@redwood.ai. Support triggers a job that packages logs for the requested window, applies the agreed redaction rules, and either uploads to a customer-provided bucket or places the archive on our secure SFTP server for pickup. Typical turnaround: 2-3 business days for <30 day windows; expedited processes available under emergency SLA.
- SIEM integration: we provide a pre-built Splunk HEC config and a Datadog HTTPS forwarder. Rate limits and batching controls live in the Console (recommend batch size = 5k events).

Action items:
- [Monica] Attach policy, sample extract, and mapping sheet (done).
- [Rishi] Confirm API endpoint for on-demand exports and add ephemeral token TTL (I set 6 hours as default — confirm).
- [Sean] Send the short evidence statement to Alyssa for SIG inclusion.

Monica Patel
Sr. Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

3) Is the on-demand export API documented somewhere public/private? If private, can you share the internal API endpoint or the Console export flow link so our engineering team can review integration work?

If you can get answers to the three items by EOD 5/06 we should be able to include this in our vendor pack. Also — if there are any export records or proof of prior customer exports we can add as evidence, that would speed the review.

Thanks again — Alyssa
